problem.text: Extending the class of bipartite graphs known to satisfy Sidorenko's conjecture.

claims.text: Theorem 1.2: strongly tree-decomposable graphs are Sidorenko; Theorem 1.3 and 3.1: subdivisions of cliques, of Sidorenko graphs, and of any graph satisfying a KNRS-type bound are Sidorenko; Theorem 1.4: H times C_{2k} is Sidorenko when H is; Problem 1.5 asks for the subdivision of an arbitrary graph.

assumptions.text: Entropy of branching random walks for tree decompositions; Fox's reduction to hosts with bounded maximum degree (Lemma 3.3); locally dense graphs and the KNRS conjecture for the subdivision theorem.

methods.text: Branching random walks and entropy; codegree averaging in large minimum-degree subgraphs; an auxiliary graph psi_K(G) for Cartesian products.

limitations.text: Problem 1.5 is stated as outside the reach of current methods; the subdivision results need a KNRS-type input for the base graph.

relevance.text: Problem 1.5 is a consequence of the girth-six candidate of this exploration, because every 1-subdivision of a simple graph has girth at least six; the KNRS link is the known route toward it.
